# Cedarbrook bike-lane pilot — fictional browser test

This is a fictional example for testing CrowdLens. Cedarbrook and the people below are invented. It is not a real municipal proposal or a prediction.

Cedarbrook proposes an eight-week protected bike-lane pilot on Main Street. One parking lane would become a bike lane. Deliveries would use two signed loading bays. The city has not decided whether the pilot will become permanent.

Four participants provided these statements:
- Maya Chen, a resident who cycles to work: "I support the pilot if the intersections are protected. I currently avoid Main Street because traffic feels unsafe."
- Leo Martin, a Main Street shop owner: "I am concerned about losing short-stay parking. I could support a trial if loading access remains reliable and customer visits are measured."
- Priya Shah, a resident with limited mobility: "Accessible pickup spaces and a clear pedestrian path must remain. A bike lane alone does not answer those needs."
- Daniel Brooks, the city's transport planner: "The pilot is reversible. We will publish counts of cyclists, deliveries, customer visits and accessibility complaints before considering a permanent change."

The four statements are qualitative and do not represent all residents. There is no survey, crash count, business revenue measurement or final decision in this source. Do not invent those facts. Simulated conversations are generated output, not new documentary evidence.

action_args.content: I support the Cedarbrook eight-week pilot if the intersections are protected. I currently avoid Main Street because traffic feels unsafe. A protected lane on Main Street could make my commute viable again, and I would value clear intersection treatment during the trial.

I am concerned about losing short-stay parking on Main Street, but I could support the Cedarbrook trial if loading access remains reliable and customer visits are measured during the eight-week pilot. Two signed loading bays are a start; I would like clarity on delivery windows.

Accessible pickup spaces and a clear pedestrian path must remain during the Cedarbrook pilot. A bike lane alone does not answer those needs. I would like to see how accessibility is protected alongside the bike-lane design before the eight weeks begin.

The Cedarbrook bike-lane pilot is reversible. We will publish counts of cyclists, deliveries, customer visits and accessibility complaints before considering any permanent change. The eight-week timeline exists to gather those measurements, not to predetermine an outcome.

Round 1 opens with the four participants restating their positions: Maya (Cyclist) presses for protected intersections, Leo (ShopOwner) raises loading-bay reliability and customer-visit measurement, Priya (AccessibilityAdvocate) flags accessible pickup and pedestrian path, Daniel (TransportPlanner) reaffirms reversibility and published counts. No survey, crash, revenue or permanence data is introduced.
action_args.title: Pilot design discussion: intersection protection and loading bays

action_args.content: Leo (ShopOwner) asks Daniel (TransportPlanner) for written delivery-window rules at the two signed loading bays, framing it as a condition for not opposing the trial. Daniel indicates windows can be clarified without changing the reversible pilot structure.
action_args.title: Shop owner requests clearer delivery-window specification

No survey, crash, revenue or permanence data is introduced.

Leo (ShopOwner) asks Daniel (TransportPlanner) for written delivery-window rules at the two signed loading bays, framing it as a condition for not opposing the trial. Daniel indicates windows can be clarified without changing the reversible pilot structure.

Watching the Cedarbrook bike-lane pilot on Main Street. My baseline: I currently detour off Main because traffic feels unsafe mixing with cars in the door zone and at unprotected intersections. I can support this pilot if the intersections are actually protected (concrete or planters, not just paint) and if cyclist counts are published before any talk of permanence. Reversible + measured = worth trying. Placed for permanence = no. That's my one commuter data point. #MainStreet #CedarbrookPilot

Round 2: Daniel (TransportPlanner) confirms the published counts will cover cyclists, deliveries, customer visits and accessibility complaints, gathered over the eight weeks. Maya (Cyclist) accepts the measurement-based approach if intersection protection is in place. Leo (ShopOwner) accepts conditional on reliable loading and the customer-visit count being shared. Priya (AccessibilityAdvocate) accepts conditional on accessible pickup and pedestrian path being preserved. No decision is made on permanence.
action_args.title: Measurement scope agreed, no permanence decision

action_args.content: Priya (AccessibilityAdvocate) raises a specific design question: width and obstruction rules for the pedestrian path adjacent to the bike lane. Maya (Cyclist) supports adequate pedestrian width. Daniel (TransportPlanner) notes this can be addressed within the reversible pilot design without changing scope.
action_args.title: Accessibility advocate emphasizes pedestrian-path design detail

Maya (Cyclist) accepts the measurement-based approach if intersection protection is in place. Leo (ShopOwner) accepts conditional on reliable loading and the customer-visit count being shared. Priya (AccessibilityAdvocate) accepts conditional on accessible pickup and pedestrian path being preserved. No decision is made on permanence.

Priya (AccessibilityAdvocate) raises a specific design question: width and obstruction rules for the pedestrian path adjacent to the bike lane. Maya (Cyclist) supports adequate pedestrian width. Daniel (TransportPlanner) notes this can be addressed within the reversible pilot design without changing scope.

Watching the Cedarbrook 8-week pilot closely. Main Street commuter here — I currently detour because the corridor doesn't feel safe enough to mix with traffic. I can support a reversible pilot IF the intersections are actually protected (not paint-only). What does "protected" mean in the Cedarbrook design — concrete, planters, delineators? And when will pre-pilot cyclist counts be published so we have a real baseline? Support is not endorsement of permanence. #CedarbrookPilot #MainStreet
